recent_posts.title: Why quantifying education with dashboards and metrics fails children
recent_posts.summary: Quantifying education through dashboards and standardized testing—whether analog or AI-powered—misses what matters most: deep engagement, holistic learning, and meaningful relationships. The atomization of skills (like reducing reading to discrete tasks instead of whole novels) has led to declining student interest and teacher burnout. High-stakes testing regimes from Texas to Australia show how metrics-driven approaches narrow curricula and erode creativity. AI education tools often amplify these same failures by over-optimizing measurable outcomes while neglecting human connection. Effective learning combines technology with community, creativity, and the freedom to become absorbed in meaningful work.

recent_posts.title: Why AI code generation creates false productivity and doesn't replace software engineering skills
recent_posts.summary: "Vibe coding" refers to generating large amounts of AI-generated code without human review, creating a false sense of productivity similar to gambling addiction's "dark flow." Research shows developers using AI tools overestimate their speed by nearly 40%, while the code produced is often too complex to maintain or contains hidden bugs. Despite industry hype and failed predictions from tech leaders about AI replacing developers, human skills in software engineering, abstraction, and problem-solving remain essential and irreplaceable.

recent_posts.title: How To Use AI for the Ancient Art of Close Reading – fast.ai
recent_posts.summary: Close reading, an ancient analytical technique for deep textual analysis, can be enhanced using Large Language Models. LLMs enable readers to ask clarifying questions, explore tangential topics, and personalize content while reading. The SolveIt platform combines elements of ChatGPT, Jupyter, and other tools to facilitate this process through incremental steps and immediate feedback. Demonstrations show reading a book and analyzing academic papers with LLMs, using techniques like context management, spaced repetition with Anki flashcards, and generating chapter summaries. While the tooling is still evolving and requires some technical setup, grounding and web search capabilities help mitigate hallucination concerns.

recent_posts.title: Chronic boredom harms children just as it harms adults
recent_posts.summary: Chronic boredom harms adults through stress and disengagement, yet society glorifies it for children. Research shows boredom differs from unstructured play—children need intellectual stimulation, not understimulation. Common misconceptions conflate challenge level with time spent and external pressure, leading to false binaries about screen time and early learning. Skills like reading and coding open new worlds for children. The solution to overscheduling isn't forced boredom but providing free time alongside appropriately challenging, engaging opportunities tailored to each child's interests.

recent_posts.title: A Guide to Solveit Features – fast.ai
recent_posts.summary: Solveit is an interactive development platform that combines code execution, AI assistance, and documentation in a unified workspace. Unlike traditional code generators that produce large blocks of unfamiliar code, Solveit encourages incremental development where you write and understand code piece by piece with AI guidance. The platform features persistent Python kernels, real-time collaboration, Monaco editor integration, and tools for AI interaction including context management, function exposure, and web search. It supports hosting web applications directly from your instance, exporting code to reusable modules, and includes advanced features like super completions, screenshot analysis, and file system operations. Built on a Jupyter-like architecture with dialogs instead of notebooks, Solveit emphasizes learning through doing while maintaining full control over your development environment.

recent_posts.title: Build to Last – fast.ai
recent_posts.summary: Jeremy Howard interviews Chris Lattner (creator of LLVM, Swift, and Mojo) about software craftsmanship in the age of AI. They discuss concerns about developers abandoning fundamental practices in favor of AI-generated code without understanding. Lattner emphasizes building from first principles, architectural thinking, dogfooding, and tight iteration loops. Both advocate using AI as a tool for learning and exploration rather than a replacement for understanding, warning that over-reliance on AI code generation may hinder career development and create unmaintainable software. The conversation explores how to maintain craftsmanship while leveraging AI effectively.

recent_posts.title: Let’s Build the GPT Tokenizer: A Complete Guide to Tokenization in LLMs – fast.ai
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive technical walkthrough of tokenization in large language models, covering the byte-pair encoding (BPE) algorithm from first principles. Explains why tokenization causes common LLM issues like poor spelling and arithmetic, demonstrates building a GPT-style tokenizer from scratch with complete Python implementations, and compares different approaches including GPT-2, GPT-4, and SentencePiece. Includes hands-on exercises for implementing your own tokenizer and understanding the trade-offs between byte-level and code-point-level tokenization strategies.

recent_posts.title: How to Solve it With Code course now available – fast.ai
recent_posts.summary: Fast.ai founder Jeremy Howard announces a new course called 'How to Solve it With Code' that teaches the 'solveit method' - an approach to using AI that empowers developers rather than replacing them. The method focuses on human agency and learning, contrasting with current industry trends of automation. The course includes a software platform, community access, and ongoing research, designed for experienced coders, AI practitioners, and data scientists who want to harness AI while maintaining creative control and personal growth.

recent_posts.title: fasttransform: Reversible Pipelines Made Simple – fast.ai
recent_posts.summary: Fasttransform is a new Python library designed to make data transformations reversible and extensible using the power of multiple dispatch. It simplifies the debugging process in machine learning by allowing transformations to be easily reversed, helping users to better understand their data. The library handles different data types efficiently and can be applied to various fields, including images, text, and time series data.

recent_posts.title: What AI can tell us about microscope slides – fast.ai
recent_posts.summary: Current advancements in computational pathology (CPath) are using machine learning models trained on diverse tissue images to improve cancer diagnosis, treatment prediction, and more. Notable models like Prov-GigaPath and UNI have achieved state-of-the-art results. Challenges include the need for large, diverse datasets and adapting models for clinical use. Continued development and data partnerships are key to advancing this field.
